q: How long does Revolution wait for a network share before giving up on a file?
a: 8 seconds for every read, open and size check on a network share. If the share hasn't answered by then, the clip is treated as offline (the red offline mark and the Media Offline picture, as for a missing file) instead of the app freezing. Files on local disks are read exactly as before.

q: Why did all my server clips go offline at once?
a: Once one file on a share has timed out (8 seconds without an answer), Revolution treats that whole share as down for 30 seconds, so its other clips go offline at once instead of each waiting 8 seconds. That keeps a project with many clips on a sleeping NAS quick to open. They come back online by themselves when the share answers again.

q: How do offline network clips come back?
a: By themselves: Revolution looks at the project's files every few seconds and whenever its window comes back to the front (Settings ▸ Media ▸ Automatically refresh growing files, on by default). A message says how many clips are back online; nothing needs relinking and there is no undo step.

q: I turned off automatic refresh for growing files; how do I bring share clips back after an outage?
a: With Settings ▸ Media ▸ Automatically refresh growing files off, Revolution doesn't look again by itself: use Link Media (`media.linkMedia`) on the offline clips, or close and reopen the project.

q: Does the network timeout make my local media slower?
a: No. The 8-second limit and the 30-second share-down rule apply only to files on network shares; files on local disks are read exactly as before.

q: Is the Media Offline from a dropped share different from a deleted file?
a: It looks the same: the red offline mark and the Media Offline picture. The difference is what happens next: when the share answers again, the clips come back online by themselves, without relinking.

q: Does the 30-second rule mean my clips stay offline for 30 seconds even if the server is back sooner?
a: The share is treated as down for 30 seconds after a timeout, so its clips are offline at least that long; after that Revolution's regular look at the project's files (every few seconds, and whenever the window comes back to the front) brings them back online once the share answers.

q: Do I need to undo anything after clips go offline and come back?
a: No. Going offline and coming back online are not edits, so there is no undo step and nothing to relink; a message just says 3 clip(s) went offline or 3 clip(s) are back online.

q: And will the app hang meanwhile?
a: No. Each read, open or size check on the share gets 8 seconds; after that the clip shows as offline and Revolution treats the whole share as down for 30 seconds, so nothing waits on the dead server. Still being built: the last few checks the interface does itself (audio waveforms, the Link Media preview) are being moved to background threads.
